cards.explanation: The answer is True. Luke says, “They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.” (Luke 24:14) Seven miles is a long stretch of road, and these two had plenty on their minds. If I walked that far with a friend, I'd run out of things to say by mile two and start humming.

Their eyes are kept from recognizing Him. Luke says, “…their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.” (Luke 24:16) Jesus is right there beside them and they don't know it's Him. The text doesn't tell us more than that. You know when someone waves at you at the gym and you have no idea who it is? Same problem, much bigger moment.

The word is sadness. Luke says, “They stood still, with sadness on their faces.” (Luke 24:17) They had just been talking about everything that happened to Jesus. I think a face that heavy says a lot before anybody opens their mouth. Those two weren't hiding a thing.

Cleopas asks if He's the only visitor who hasn't heard the news. He says, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?” (Luke 24:18) I think he's amazed that the stranger hasn't heard. I bet those days felt huge to the two of them.

They describe Him as a prophet powerful in speech and action. They say, “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.” (Luke 24:19) Powerful in what He said and powerful in what He did. That's how these two sum up Jesus of Nazareth, friends. It's a big description, and they say it with sad faces.

The answer is their chief priests and rulers. The two say, “Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.” (Luke 24:20) That's how they tell it to the stranger. It's a heavy part of the story. I think the sadness on their faces fits.

The word is redeem. They say, “But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel.” (Luke 24:21) Redeem is the word Luke gives us. Notice they say hoping, and that tells you where their hearts were on that road. It's a sad little sentence.

The answer is True. They say, “…it is the third day since these things took place.” (Luke 24:21) They're counting days out loud. I think when your heart is heavy, you notice every one that passes. I bet these two were keeping track.

The angels told the women that Jesus was alive. The two say the women “…had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.” (Luke 24:23) The women didn't find His body, and the angels said He was alive. That's the news the two bring up, friends. They share it right alongside their sadness.

The answer is False. The companions found the tomb just as the women had described, and the two say, “But Him they did not see.” (Luke 24:24) So the tomb matched the women's story, but the companions did not see Jesus. I think these two were still carrying a lot of questions on that road.

The two words are suffer and glory. Jesus asks, “Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?” (Luke 24:26) He puts it as a question, and He's pointing them to what the Christ was to go through. The suffering comes first and then the glory, in that order. That's a lot to take in on a seven mile walk.

Jesus begins with Moses and all the Prophets. Luke says, “And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.” (Luke 24:27) From there, He explains what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself. I'd pay a month of cookie money to have heard that walk.

The word is beg. They pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.” (Luke 24:29) Pleaded is about as close to beg as you get. They didn't just say a polite goodbye. I think they weren't ready for that walk to end.

The answer is False. Verse 28 says He seemed to be going farther, but after they pleaded with Him, “So He went in to stay with them.” (Luke 24:29) He accepted the invitation. The walk ended at the table.

Their eyes are opened and they know Him. Luke says, “Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus…” (Luke 24:31) Earlier on the road, their eyes were kept from recognizing Him, and now that has changed. It all happens at the table, as He breaks the bread and gives it to them.

Their hearts were burning within them. They ask each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?” (Luke 24:32) They say it after they recognize Him. Looking back, they could tell something was happening inside them all along. I think that's a good feeling to look back on.
The answer is False. They “…got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem.” (Luke 24:33) No sleeping on it and no waiting for morning. They went that very hour.

The answer is True. When the two get there, they find the Eleven and those with them gathered together and saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!” (Luke 24:34) Simon is a man the text names here without saying more. I think the two came with their own story and walked into one.
